title: How does it feel to live in a bendy body?
description:
Can being ultra-flexible be a sign of a health condition? Hypermobility Spectrum Disorders (HSD) cause joint hypermobility - which is when your joints have greater than normal range of motion. It means you might be able to bend your body in ways others can’t, but it can come with lots of health issues including digestive problems, joint pain and fatigue. It can take years to be diagnosed with HSD.

We hear from Ana Simmons about how hypermobility affects her everyday life. And, BBC reporter Ella Kipling, who also has HSD, tells us why it’s so hard to get a diagnosis.

summaryEn: This episode of What in the World explores Hypermobility Spectrum Disorder (HSD) and its impact on daily life. Host Hannah Gelbart talks with guest Anna Simmons and BBC reporter Ella Kipling, both of whom live with hypermobility conditions. They explain that hypermobility is caused by connective tissue abnormalities and goes far beyond joint flexibility, causing chronic pain, fatigue, clumsiness from impaired proprioception, racing heart, and digestive issues. Getting diagnosed is notoriously difficult, with University of Edinburgh research indicating an average wait time of around two decades. Because there is no cure, individuals manage their symptoms through physiotherapy, strength training, pacing activities, practicing self-compassion, and supporting one another in the community.
